summary: The Ratepayer Bill of Rights Act of 2026 establishes a set of ten specific rights for electricity and water ratepayers regarding large data centers. It applies to data centers or related groups under common ownership with a peak electricity demand of at least 50 megawatts or a water withdrawal of at least 100,000 gallons per day. The bill requires public disclosure of resource use, infrastructure costs, and financial agreements, prohibits ratepayers from subsidizing data center costs, mandates independent assessments for water and electric reliability, requires public notice and meetings before decisions are finalized, creates enforcement mechanisms, and protects whistleblowers.

affected_groups.effect: Gain the right to know data center resource demands, cost impacts, and agreements, and are protected from paying for or subsidizing data center infrastructure costs.
affected_groups.group: Ratepayers (households, farmers, ranchers, small businesses, schools, and hospitals)

affected_groups.effect: Must publicly disclose resource use and infrastructure costs, pay all project-driven costs, sign binding cost-recovery agreements, post financial security, and undergo independent reliability and water assessments.
affected_groups.group: Large data center owners and operators

affected_groups.effect: Receive rights to monitoring, notice, and fair compensation if a covered data center harms their water supply, and protection against data centers drawing from overdrawn aquifers.
affected_groups.group: Private well owners and rural water systems

affected_groups.effect: Receive protections from retaliation if they report violations of the Act.

key_provisions: Requires large data centers to disclose projected and actual electricity and water use, sources, wastewater discharge, infrastructure costs, rate effects, and public support.

Prohibits shifting project-driven costs to protected ratepayers (such as households, farms, small businesses, schools, and hospitals) and requires companies to pay all costs, sign cost-recovery agreements, and post financial security.

Mandates independent assessments before water-service commitments to ensure sufficient water remains for households, agriculture, and existing businesses, and prevents data centers from receiving priority over households, hospitals, or schools during water emergencies.
Requires independent assessments before electric-service commitments to confirm data centers can be served without reducing grid reliability for existing customers.
Grants affected residents the right to at least 60 days' notice and a local public meeting before final decisions, with related studies made available at least 30 days in advance.
Prohibits hiding required public information through contracts, confidentiality claims, or trade secrets, and mandates posting information to a searchable public database.

Directs federal agencies including FERC, DOE, EPA, and the Department of Labor to issue rules and enforce compliance within their existing jurisdictions, while allowing state, tribal, and local authorities to adopt stronger protections.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for civil penalties.
Exact timelines for federal agencies to issue final rules.
Detailed mechanics of how the searchable public database will be funded or maintained.
